DYNAMATIC TECHNOLOGIES Q1: METALLURGY SEGMENT RECOVERY GAINS MOMENTUM 🔩📈

• 🔩 Metallurgy revenue grew 15.7% YoY to ₹106.3 Cr, driven by a recovery in demand at Erla, Germany

• 💰 EBITDA surged 133% YoY to ₹4.0 Cr; EBITDA margin improved to 3.7% from 1.9%

• 📊 EBIT turned positive at ₹0.7 Cr versus a ₹1.5 Cr loss last year, with EBIT margin improving to 0.6% from -1.7%

• 🇩🇪 Early demand recovery in Europe and higher volumes supported margin improvement

• ✈️ Focus remains on aerospace, defence and specialised engineering applications to improve profitability

• ⚙️ Strategy centered on operational efficiency, cost discipline and strengthening long-term competitiveness

DYNAMATIC TECHNOLOGIES Q1: HYDRAULICS SEGMENT MARGINS SURGE ⚙️📈

• 🚜 Hydraulics revenue grew 9.4% YoY to ₹116.0 Cr, led by strong tractor demand from Indian OEMs and steady aftermarket sales

• 💰 EBITDA jumped 303% YoY to ₹14.5 Cr; EBITDA margin expanded sharply to 12.5% from 3.4%

• 📊 EBIT surged to ₹10.7 Cr from ₹0.4 Cr; EBIT margin improved to 9.2% from 0.3%

• 🇮🇳 Margin improvement driven by product mix optimisation and benefits from the UK restructuring

• 🏭 Transfer of operations from Swindon to Bengaluru and product line rationalisation progressing, improving long-term competitiveness

• 🔧 Strategy focused on enhancing manufacturing efficiency, global integration and expanding OEM, industrial and aftermarket presence

DYNAMATIC TECHNOLOGIES Q1: AEROSPACE SEGMENT DELIVERS STRONG GROWTH ✈️📈

• ✈️ Aerospace revenue rose 17% YoY to ₹202.3 Cr, driven by commercial aerospace & defence program execution

• 💰 EBITDA increased 20.5% YoY to ₹48.2 Cr; EBITDA margin improved to 23.8% from 23.1%

• 📊 EBIT grew 23.5% YoY to ₹36.0 Cr; EBIT margin expanded to 17.8% from 16.8%

• 🏭 Growth supported by ramp-up of detail parts manufacturing at Dynamatic Manufacturing's India facility

• 🛩️ Outlook remains strong with increasing opportunities in commercial aviation and defence, backed by a healthy order book

• 🚀 Strategy focused on expanding participation in high-value aerospace programs, advanced manufacturing, defence & unmanned technologies, and strengthening global OEM partnerships

DYNAMATIC TECHNOLOGIES Q1: AEROSPACE REMAINS KEY GROWTH DRIVER ✈️🚀

• ✈️ Aerospace remained the largest revenue contributor, driven by strong execution across key commercial aerospace programs

• 🛩️ Airbus A220 doors program progressed steadily, strengthening the company's position in the global aerospace supply chain

• 🏭 Improved product mix supported by ramp-up in sheet metal and detail parts at subsidiary Dynamatic Manufacturing Ltd

• ⚙️ Hydraulics business maintained strong momentum with healthy demand from domestic OEMs and industrial customers; Swindon-to-Bengaluru business transfer progressing well

• 🔩 Metallurgy business focused on higher-value products for the European automotive market while expanding into aerospace, defence and specialised engineering applications

NRB BEARINGS Q1: EXPANDS AEROSPACE & DEFENCE PRESENCE ✈️🛡️

• ✈️ Completed acquisition of Mahant Tool Room, adding AS9100D Aerospace Certification and strengthening aerospace & defence capabilities

• 🚀 Entered aerospace & defence applications through MTR, including precision components and mission-critical products

• 🚗 Launched bearings for BMW's next-generation hybrid steering platform; expanding presence in Mercedes-Benz premium EVs

• 🌍 Added new industrial customers including HAAS Automation (USA) and JCB (UK)

• 🛩️ Secured its first aerospace & defence bearing order for a mission-critical application in the Sukhoi-30 aircraft

• 📈 Consolidated revenue grew 19.2% YoY, reflecting strong execution and momentum across automotive, industrial and aerospace businesses

TRANSWORLD SHIPPING: SIGNS MOA TO SELL VESSEL 'SSL BRAHMAPUTRA' 🚢

• 🤝 Signed a Memorandum of Agreement (MoA) with Avana Logistek Limited

• 🚢 Agreement is for the sale of vessel M.V. SSL Brahmaputra

• 💰 Sale consideration is US$ 11.4 million

• 📅 Transaction is expected to be completed one day prior to vessel delivery, as per the agreement terms

🟢 Impact: Positive – The vessel sale is expected to strengthen liquidity and support fleet optimization/capital allocation.

DR. REDDY'S: TERMINATES DISTRIBUTION & PROMOTION AGREEMENT WITH NOVARTIS INDIA 💊

• 📄 Dr. Reddy's has terminated its February 11, 2022 agreement with Novartis India Ltd. (NIL) for the distribution and promotion of select brands in India

• 🔄 The termination follows a change in the controlling shareholding of Novartis India

• 📦 Dr. Reddy's will continue to commercialize the covered brands until September 30, 2026

🟡 Impact: Neutral – The agreement ends due to a change in ownership at Novartis India, with transition arrangements in place until September 2026.

HONASA (MAMAEARTH): DUBAI CASSATION COURT DISMISSES APPEALS IN RSM CASE ⚖️

• ⚖️ Dubai Cassation Court dismissed appeals filed by both Honasa and RSM General Trading LLC, upholding the earlier Court of Appeal judgment

• 💰 The Dubai judgment continues to award AED 1.71 million to RSM towards material and moral damages; RSM's claim for AED 45 million was rejected

• 🇮🇳 Honasa clarified that the Indian Arbitral Tribunal had earlier ruled in its favour, restraining RSM from pursuing claims against the company before Dubai courts and directing RSM to pay any damages recovered from Honasa under the Dubai proceedings

• 🛡️ Based on the Indian arbitral award, the company expects no financial impact from the Dubai court judgment

🟡 Impact: Neutral – While the Dubai court upheld the earlier judgment, Honasa maintains that the Indian arbitral award protects it from any financial impact.

Initial jobless claims in the United States fell to 199,000 for the week ending August 1, below the 205,000 expected by economists, indicating that the labor market remains resilient. However, continuing jobless claims rose to 1.801 million, exceeding forecasts of 1.789 million, suggesting that while layoffs remain limited, unemployed workers are taking slightly longer to find new jobs.

Separately, unit labor costs increased 1.3% in the second quarter, below expectations of 2.1%, easing concerns about wage-driven inflation. The combination of lower labor costs and higher productivity could support the case for moderating inflation while maintaining economic growth.

Financial Performance
- Gross Loan Portfolio ₹14,457.2 Cr (+18.0% YoY | +3.2% QoQ).

- Total Income ₹670.6 Cr (+20.0% YoY | +5.0% QoQ).

Profitability & Efficiency
- Cost-to-Income Ratio 53.7% (-721 bps YoY).
- ROA improved to 2.3% (vs 0.2% YoY).
- ROE improved to 11.2% (vs 0.9% YoY).
- Average Cost of Borrowing 10.13% (vs 10.27% FY26).

Asset Quality
- GNPA 3.70% (-115 bps YoY | -19 bps QoQ).
- NNPA 1.05% (-53 bps YoY | -10 bps QoQ).
- Credit Cost 2.6%, below guidance.
- Asset quality improved across metrics.

Business Highlights
- Highest-ever Q1 disbursements.
- Non-JLG portfolio reached 24%.
- SME individual loan book expanded.
- Gold loan disbursements commenced.
- Partnership with Muthoot Fincorp.
- Digital collections increased to 40.5%.
- Active customer base 32.5 lakh.
- Network of 1,671 branches.
- Employee strength 15,639.

Capital & Rating
- Capital Adequacy Ratio 24.9%.
- CRISIL upgraded rating to AA-/Stable.
- Commercial Paper rating reaffirmed at A1+.

Management Commentary
- Strong loan growth momentum.
- Record Q1 disbursements achieved.
- Asset quality improved.
- Borrowing costs declined.
- Focus on portfolio diversification.
- Digital collections gaining traction.
- Capital position remains comfortable.

Key Positives
- Strong loan book growth.
- Record disbursement performance.
- Sharp PAT recovery.
- Improving asset quality.
- Lower credit cost.
- Better profitability ratios.
- Strong capital adequacy.
- Credit rating upgrade.
- Digital collection momentum.

Key Concerns
- Microfinance sector volatility.
- Credit quality monitoring remains important.
- Execution of portfolio diversification.

Key Monitorables
- Loan book growth.
- Asset quality trends.
- Credit costs.
- NIM sustainability.
- ROA & ROE improvement.
- Non-JLG portfolio expansion.
- Collection efficiency.

Impact
- Positive.
- Strong operational performance.
- Significant profitability improvement.
- Asset quality continues to strengthen.
- Well-capitalized for future growth.

Key Takeaway
- Muthoot Microfin delivered an excellent Q1 with record disbursements, strong loan growth, a sharp recovery in profitability and continued improvement in asset quality. Lower borrowing costs, better operating efficiency, portfolio diversification and a stronger capital position provide a solid foundation for sustainable growth.

**CITI on Hindalco
Neutral, TP Rs 1175**

Novelis reported 1Q adj E

BITDA at $516m vs. $416m – lower scrap prices and cost efficiencies helped.

Adj EBITDA/t: $563 vs. $544 in 4Q, $432 last year.

EBITDA includes $47m insurance recovery relating to business interruption (excluding this, EBITDA would be $469m, Citi est $460m).
Oswego impact: ~33k on volumes, EBITDA ~$29m.

Normalized EBITDA/t $525: excluding Oswego fires/insurance recovery. Volumes fell ~5% yoy to 916kt.

**Key highlights:**
(1) EBITDA/t upsides: As Oswego normalizes, tariff impact should taper down in a few quarters. Further, mgmt is confident about Bay Minette achieving EBITDA/t of $1,000.
(2) Insurance: Cash flow impact from the disruption to be $1.8bn vs. $1.7bn earlier ($1.4bn to date), insurance recoveries of ~$1.2bn, expect meaningful insurance recoveries going forward (1Q $300m, FY26 $90m).
(3) Cashflows/leverage:Net debt: $7.9bn vs. $6.7bn in Mar26; net D/EBITDA 4.5x vs. 4.1x. Mgmt expects working capital to normalize, net D/EBITDA at <4x by end FY28.

**CLSA on Hindalco
O-P, TP Rs 1240**

Novelis’ core profitability of US$525/t was in line, while adj Ebitda/t of US$563 was above.

Where are Electric Vehicles (EVs) selling the most, in India?

launches include 25 Downtown Tower 5 (Oct/Nov), 25 Estate (Q4), the Thane project 25 Chalet (Q4) and Chembur Phase 2 (luxury, mid and commercial). OCs expected this year span the last tower of Rising City Phase 1 (Ghatkopar), the North and Central towers of 25 South, Bel Air / Tower 1C at Hubtown Premiere (Andheri West), and multiple buildings at Hubtown Polaris (Ahmedabad) and North Star (Mehsana).

**Guidance: FY27 pre-sales of ~INR 6,000 Cr (H2-weighted on launch timing) and collections of ~INR 3,000 Cr. Annuity/commercial income to begin only after ~2.5 years; focus stays on the MMR region, with new projects pursued on an asset-light/partnership basis.**

**Outlook:** Hubtown is positioning around three levers, monetising a premium Mumbai-centric portfolio, consolidating marquee assets via Hubtown 2.0, and de-leveraging towards a net-debt-free balance sheet. Reported earnings will stay lumpy under project-completion accounting, and historically sub-10% ROE should improve as refinancing lowers the interest burden, price rises stick and deliveries pick up through H2. At CMP, the stock trades at ~1.2x P/B (book value ~INR 184), a modest multiple against a ~INR 11,583 Cr contracted pipeline yet to be recognised and combined post-merger GDV pegged at over INR 1 lakh Cr, though realisation of that embedded value hinges on NCLT approvals, execution and OC timelines.

**Hubtown Q1 Concall Snippets

Hubtown 2.0 Unlocks A New Growth Chapter**
Q1 FY27 marks the beginning of an inflection year for **Hubtown Limited (BSE: 532799; NSE: HUBTOWN; Market Cap: ~INR 2,660 Cr)**. Pre-sales of ₹535 Cr, up 8% year on year, demonstrate continued pricing power across their premium and ultra-luxury portfolio. This performance is anchored in a land moat that took 35 years to build. With ₹11,583 Cr of contracted balance revenue and three merger schemes progressing, FY27 is the year Hubtown's investment thesis begins to manifest in reported numbers.

**The Embedded Pipeline: Value Yet To Be Recognised**

The least understood part of the story is the embedded book. Across ongoing developments (including the to-be-merged entities), Hubtown has cumulative pre-sales of ~INR 14,835 Cr, of which ~INR 8,352 Cr is already collected and only ~INR 3,252 Cr recognised as revenue so far. That leaves ~INR 11,583 Cr of contracted pipeline still to flow through the P&L as projects complete and hand over, much of it already collected and simply awaiting the final milestone. Beyond this, Hubtown carries ~34 msf of planned development across 25 Chalet, 25 Estate, Season Phase 2, Sunstream City, Hubtown Commercial and Rising City, a multi-year growth runway to layer on top of a ~13 msf delivery track record built over three decades. The company was also the No. 2 top-selling residential developer in South Mumbai during the quarter.

**Hubtown 2.0: Consolidating The Marquee Assets**

The transformative piece is Hubtown 2.0, the amalgamation that consolidates the marquee luxury projects (25 Downtown, 25 West and 25 South, effective 1 April 2025, subject to approvals) into the listed entity. The first two schemes have received key approvals and await final NCLT sanction, while the third is progressing through the regulatory process.

__Absorbing 4 promoter-group entities via NCLT to unify assets and eliminate cross-holdings.__

**Saicharan Consultancy:** Merging to boost Hubtown’s revenue share by 21.17% in the Ghatkopar Rising City project.

**25 West Realty:** Merging the luxury Bandra West asset to unlock a lifetime revenue potential of ₹6,000 crore.

**25 South:** Absorbing the 25 South Premium project with a Total Carpet area of 0.96 msf

**25 Downtown:** Large scale project in South Mumbai, in terms of revenue and area under development and total development of ~3.68 msf.

On completion, the ongoing development portfolio expands from ~7.13 msf to over 34 msf, backed by ~347 acres of landholding, with combined GDV expected to exceed INR 1 lakh Cr over time. Post-merger promoter holding moves to the ~68-70% range, as the schemes are issued against equity.

**Deleveraging And Refinancing In Motion**

Total borrowings have been cut to ~INR 5,181 Cr, of which INR 3,950 Cr sits in the to-be-merged companies and is project-linked and self-liquidating, funded directly by project cash flows. Legacy bank, NBFC and foreign-fund debt has been fully retired, and the company targets a net-debt-free balance sheet by FY2031. Management noted refinancing options improved sharply over the last quarter and it is looking to refinance ~INR 2,800 Cr of high-cost debt currently carrying 14-20% rates, with substantial savings expected once term sheets are finalised. All project surpluses remain ring-fenced towards debt repayment before any redeployment. On the capital side, enabling resolutions are in place for a preferential issue, QIP and FCCB (~INR 1,400 Cr / USD 150 Mn), with management preferring a single tranche once markets improve. Two promoter pledges remain outstanding, with release targeted within FY27.

**Pricing And Demand Hold Firm At The Top End**

Luxury demand and walk-ins stayed strong through a seasonally soft Q1, while mid-segment walk-ins were muted but conversion remained healthy. The higher floors (51st to 85th) of 25 Downtown will open strategically from October at premium pricing, with the typical higher-versus-lower floor gap running 30-40%, while 25 West has already risen INR 30,000-40,000/sq ft over ~1.5 years.

GOLDMAN SACHS ON UNITED SPIRITS

Recommendation: Accumulate | Target Price: ₹1,575

Key Takeaways:

• Potential opening of the Tamil Nadu market could be a major growth tailwind

• Tamil Nadu is India's largest spirits market, contributing around 16% of national volumes

• Drawing parallels with Andhra Pradesh, Goldman sees Tamil Nadu liberalization as an underappreciated upside opportunity

• Multiple growth tailwinds are expected to support H2 FY27 and FY28, potentially accelerating earnings growth

MORGAN STANLEY ON FINANCIALS

Key Takeaways:

• Foreign banks' incremental FCNR(B) share stood at 29.9%, far above their 4.5–5.0% deposit market share in recent years

• Incremental FCNR(B) share vs deposit market share: Private Banks: 38.3% vs 35.7%; PSU Banks: 31.6% vs 58.2%

• Banks with the biggest incremental FCNR(B) share gains include:

ICICI Bank: 13.2% vs 6.7%

Kotak Mahindra Bank: 5.9% vs 2.1%

Axis Bank: 5.7% vs 5.0%

HSBC: 21.9% vs 0.9%

Standard Chartered Bank: 6.6% vs 0.6%

CITI ON BANKS

Key Takeaways:

• Bank-level data contradicts the market narrative that PSU banks would be the primary mobilizers under the FCNR(B) scheme

• Private banks mobilized US$10.7 billion (38.3% of net inflows), broadly in line with their deposit market share

• Foreign banks contributed US$8.4 billion (30% of net inflows), led by HSBC (US$6.1 billion) and Standard Chartered (US$1.86 billion)

• Despite holding 61% of deposits and 51% of FCNR(B) market share, PSU banks captured only 31.6% of net inflows

MORGAN STANLEY ON IGI

Recommendation: Overweight
Target Price: ₹462

Key Takeaways:

• Company reiterated its long-term growth drivers

• Certification market (by volume) is expected to grow at a 17–19% CAGR during CY25–30, as per management

• LGD (Lab-Grown Diamond) wholesale pricing has remained broadly stable over the last two years

• The industry is witnessing growers adding capacity after nearly three years, indicating supply expansion ahead

**Sedemac Mechatronics - R&D-led growth story
**
Sedemac’s journey started with sensor-less commutation (SLC) - its key technology moat that helped it scale rapidly in 2W/3W starter generators. Now, the same R&D engine is being leveraged to build the next layers of growth.

1. Core business still has runway: ISG penetration could rise from 40-45% → 55-60%, while Sedemac’s market share could expand from 36-38% → 46-48% by FY29.

2. EVs become the next growth engine: Its e2W/e3W motor controllers are expected to grow at a massive ~75% CAGR, potentially reaching 10-12% market share by FY29.

3. New growth layers are getting added: Sedemac is entering power tools, LCVs, CV after-treatment & EFI systems, while its genset business (~75% market share) continues to scale.

4. Capacity is being built ahead of demand: With existing plants at >90% utilisation, two new facilities should triple capacity, while Chennai land provides further expansion optionality.

HSBC expects FY26-29 Revenue / EBITDA / PAT CAGR of ~32% / 35% / 49%, with ROCE improving to ~29%.

The backbone remains R&D (~7% of revenue) allowing Sedemac to repeatedly build new products around its core technology.

Source - HSBC
